summary: Prompt library keeps a team's saved prompts, each with blanks written like {page}. Opening one lays its blanks out as fields, a text field to type in or a dropdown to pick from, and the prompt above fills in as they change. It can't be used with a blank left empty: the empty blank turns red and says what it needs.
use: When a team asks the agent the same kinds of things and wants them worded the same way each time.
When a prompt only changes in a few places, like the page or the tone.
When some blanks have a short list of right answers, and a dropdown keeps them consistent.
When people should see the exact prompt the agent will get before it goes.
features: `prompts` each have a `title` and a `template` with blanks written as `{key}`. The list shows each template, blanks in braces, and how many blanks it has.
`blanks` describe each one: a `label`, and either a `placeholder` for a text field or `options` for a dropdown that starts on the first.
The prompt at the top fills in as the fields change: filled blanks in the accent colour, empty ones by name.
Use prompt checks every blank first. An empty one is outlined in red in the prompt and in its field, with its `error` underneath.
`onUse` gets the filled prompt, the prompt it came from and every value. The footer then says it was added, with Undo.
`open` / `onOpenChange` and `values` / `onValuesChange` let you drive which prompt is open and what is filled in.
a11y: Each prompt in the list is a button, and the back button is labelled "All prompts".
Text blanks are labelled inputs. An empty one marked by Use prompt sets `aria-invalid` and is described by its error.
Dropdown blanks are buttons named by their label and current value. Each choice is a menu item that marks the picked one with `aria-checked`, and Escape closes the menu.

From the keyboard, Enter, Space or the down arrow opens a menu with the focus on its picked item, or its first (the up arrow, on its last); the arrow keys move through it and wrap, Home and End jump to the ends, Tab closes it and moves on, and closing it gives the focus back to its button.
The filled prompt is an `aria-live="polite"` region, so changes to it are read out.

faq.q: Does it send the prompt to the agent?
faq.a: No. `onUse` gets the filled text. Put it in your composer, send it, or both.

faq.q: How is it different from Prompt starters?
faq.a: Prompt starters are one-click suggestions that fill the composer as they are. Prompt library is for saved prompts with blanks that change each time, filled in before they are used.

faq.q: Can a blank appear more than once in a prompt?
faq.a: Yes. Write the same `{key}` in each place. It has one field, and every place it appears fills in from it.
